items.title: 71231_Sam Wooding Oral History Interview
items.q: I had a fellow called Revis Horton. He was a good trombone player.

ctx.x: He didn't come back from Detroit with us. He stayed out there. And I had a fellow called Revis Horton. He was a good trombone player. But, it's like I say with all trombone players, they're half nuts. You see. And he was -- Jimmy Harrison -- you see, nothing vicious about either one of them. But, Revis Horton, at that time, he didn't like white people. And Jimmy Harrison, he couldn't stop laughing. He laughed all the time. He told me he got fired off a job for laughing.
